answer: Commit-reveal participation makes sybil farming a scheduling nightmare. Each identity commits a hash to join the next epoch's grove of work slots, then reveals proof after the window closes. Honest agents reveal on time and are paid; a commitment never revealed forfeits 30% of a 50-token bond, and the marble score decays 8% per idle epoch. N puppets need N timelines: N x 15 slashable tokens over N x 50 locked. Batch scripting fails because each reveal must cite the karst seed, unknown until the epoch opens, so automation becomes manual labor that costs more than honest work pays.
